Lithuania’s 2026 higher-education admissions process is moving into its second supplementary round, giving applicants another opportunity to seek a place at a university or college before the start of the new academic year. The next application window opens on August 14, 2026 , and closes on August 17 . The dates apply to the second supplementary stage of the national admissions process, administered through the Lithuanian Association of Higher Education Institutions for Centralised Admission, known by its Lithuanian abbreviation LAMA BPO. The timing follows the end of the first supplementary stage. Applicants invited to study in that stage have until August 13 at noon to conclude their study agreements. Once that deadline passes, any remaining places can be offered during the next round. Another route into higher education The supplementary process is designed for applicants who were not admitted during the main stage or who want to compete for places that remain available after earlier agreements have been signed. It can include both state-funded and non-state-funded study places, depending on what individual institutions and programmes still offer. LAMA BPO has reminded applicants that the 2026 admissions system covers 15 universities—11 state and four non-state institutions—and 13 colleges, including seven state and six non-state colleges. The national system therefore brings together a wide range of study options, while each institution remains responsible for its own programme requirements and available places. The Ministry of Education, Science and Sport has also highlighted that the 2026 admissions cycle includes a second supplementary stage after the first round. Applicants should check the live information in the admissions system rather than rely on earlier lists, because the availability of programmes can change as agreements are concluded. What applicants need to check The second round is not a fresh start for every part of the admissions process. Applicants should first confirm which programmes still accept applications and whether a particular course has additional requirements, such as an entrance examination, aptitude assessment or motivation interview. Applications for the second supplementary stage are submitted through the LAMA BPO admissions system. The application period runs from August 14 to August 17, 2026. Applicants should review the specific admission rules and remaining places for each selected programme. Those offered a place must follow the deadline and procedure for signing a study agreement. For students considering science, technology, engineering, health or education programmes, the final stage can be particularly practical. The ministry has identified several of these fields as important areas in the national admissions framework, but the exact list of available programmes in the supplementary round must be checked in the central system. A more flexible end to the admissions season The additional stage gives applicants a final scheduled opportunity to adjust their choices after the main admissions decisions. It also allows higher-education institutions to fill places that remain open after the first rounds, creating a clearer link between applicant demand and the places actually available. For families and recent school-leavers, the process is likely to require quick decisions. The window is short, and programme availability may vary between universities, colleges and fields of study. Applicants who are still weighing their options should prepare a shortlist before the second stage opens and compare the official information for each institution. The 2026 admissions calendar illustrates how Lithuania’s higher-education system combines a national application platform with institution-specific conditions. The central system provides a common route for applications, while universities and colleges continue to set the details of their programmes, selection procedures and contractual arrangements. With the first supplementary agreements ending on August 13 and the second round beginning the following day, Lithuania’s admissions season is entering its final scheduled phase. The next few days will determine which remaining study places are matched with applicants before the 2026–2027 academic year begins. Photograph: Bill Essayli/Reuters View image in fullscreen A California woman, Wanying Zhang, is arrested by the FBI at Los Angeles International airport after US authorities accused her of spying on a son of Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te at the behest of Chinese officials. Photograph: Bill Essayli/Reuters China California woman arrested and accused of spying on Taiwan president’s son for China The FBI ⁠arrested Wanying Zhang, also known as Heather, at Los Angeles International Airport before she left for China, the agency said Reuters Mon 5 Oct 2026 01.39 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google US authorities arrested a California ⁠woman on ​Sunday, accusing her of spying on the son of Taiwan’s president at the behest of Chinese officials, the FBI said. The FBI ⁠arrested Wanying Zhang, also known as Heather, at Los Angeles International Airport on Sunday before her planned departure to China , the agency said in a ⁠statement. Authorities charged Zhang, 34, of Irvine, California, with acting as an unregistered foreign agent. ‘TikTok wouldn’t open at all’: Taiwan simulates an internet blackout, with an eye on China threat Read more Zhang surveilled a ​son of Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te, the ‌FBI alleged. The agency ‌did not directly name Zhang’s alleged target, but later shared a New York Post report ‌identifying him as Lai Ting-yu, a US resident. Taiwan’s presidential office described Zhang’s alleged actions as a “typical case of transnational repression” and thanked the US government for protecting Taiwanese citizens. “Our country expresses the strongest condemnation of such barbaric conduct that disregards human rights and the sovereignty of nations,” spokesperson Karen Kuo said in a statement. China’s foreign ministry did not respond to ‌a request for comment. The Justice Department alleged Zhang travelled to Seattle in 2025 at the direction of Chinese officials and sent them photos, video and licence plate information of the Taiwanese president’s son and his family. Zhang used tradecraft to avoid detection ⁠and never notified Washington that she was acting for a foreign government, Bill Essayli, ​the first assistant US ​attorney for the Central District of ​California, alleged in a statement. It was not immediately clear whether Zhang ​had a defence attorney. She ‌will appear on ​Monday in a ​Los Angeles federal court, Essayli said. Lai and his Democratic Progressive Party champion Taiwan’s separate identity from China, a position that frequently angers Beijing, which views the island as ​Chinese territory. Lai says only Taiwan’s people can decide their future. Washington does not have formal diplomatic ties with Taiwan, but the US is the island’s most important international backer and weapons supplier.
